transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-08-19
- Start: 15:30 UTC
- Duration: 47m
- Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood CSM), Dr. Maya Chen, Luis Ortega, Rina Patel, Samir Das

Summary:
Quick renewal & expansion check: Silverpine is approaching contract renewal Q4, wants to add EU region (data residency for clinical data), bump Dedicated capacity by ~30% for expected holiday surge, and discuss private deployment options for a subset of controlled datasets. They also want clear SLAs for throughput and fallback behavior across regions.

Topics:
- Current utilization and forecast
- EU private vs hosted tradeoffs
- Latency / cost tradeoffs and batching/quantization suggestions
- Security/compliance: SOC2, KMS, audit logs
- Next steps: pricing, dry-run, security docs

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Gomez: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we got about 45 minutes, quick agenda is renewal numbers, region add and then technical follow-ups. Thanks Dr. Maya for being here.
[00:15] Dr. Maya Chen: Yeah hi thanks. We wanted to make sure we aligned before the exec deck next week, so happy to walk through current numbers.
[00:27] Luis Ortega: Quick context, last quarter the traffic spiked with telehealth batch jobs, we were at 85% of provisioned tokens on Warehouse-2 Dedicated pool. We expect a 20-30% bump in November and then a 10% baseline growth.
[00:45] Priya Nair: Got it, thanks Luis. Our recommended pattern for that mix is reserve ~25-30% extra baseline on Dedicated and enable burst capacity for peak times; it sounds like a fit. We can show cost diff in the worksheet.
[01:05] Rina Patel: One thing from product — we need sub-tenant isolation between patient-facing models and internal tooling. Can Redwood support multi-tenant routing and RBAC so that product teams can't access controlled models?
[01:22] Jordan Lee: Yes RBAC is supported on Dedicated and Private. For hosted we have token-level scoping but we recommend Dedicated or Private for strict separation. There was a note in our last runbook about role mapping to SAML groups.
[01:38] Samir Das: On security, SOC2 attestation is a must; also we need KMS integration for customer-managed keys. We're evaluating whether to do full Private for EU or use Hosted with VPC peering.
[01:55] Priya Nair: To make that concrete: Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you full control over keys and data egress, we can ship a private control plane with your KMS. Hosted + VPC peering can be configured but keys would be managed by Redwood unless you use our external KMS integration — which we do support. There are latency/cost trade-offs.
[02:18] Dr. Maya Chen: So cost wise, if we move some services to Private in EU, what's the rough delta vs Hosted Dedicated?
[02:30] Alex Gomez: Rough ballpark — Private has a platform fee plus infra; think ~15-25% premium depending on sizing and retention. But you gain residency and tighter compliance. We will send a line-item breakdown in the pricing worksheet.
[02:47] Luis Ortega: Also need to understand failover: if EU region is down do we want cross-region fallback to US? For clinical workflows that may violate residency, so we need policy-based routing.
[03:06] Priya Nair: Absolutely. Our smart routing policy can be configured per-route: strict residency (no fallback), residency-with-async (buffer and process in-region when available), or best-effort fallback. For your use-case sounds like strict residency for PHI.
[03:27] Rina Patel: We also want to evaluate cost controls, e.g., token caps per route and automatic model downgrade if latency/SLOs are breached.
[03:40] Priya Nair: Yep we have automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants for cost/latency SLOs and the ability to throttle requests. We'll include recommended quantization profiles for your model family in the worksheet.
[03:57] Alex Gomez: Quick callout — we've seen customers reduce per-token cost 30% by combining KV caching for templates and a 16-bit quantized mid-tier model for async tasks. Might be applicable for Silverpine triage flows.
[04:18] Dr. Maya Chen: Ok, sounds promising. On the renewal itself, leadership wants a 12-month renewal with a 30% capacity bump and an option to expand to APAC in 2027. Can we get committed pricing for that?
[04:33] Alex Gomez: Yes we can propose a committed capacity contract for Dedicated with an annual ramp and optional expansion credits for APAC. We'll put together a couple of options (12-month committed, 24-month with lower unit price).
[04:50] Luis Ortega: Are there penalties for scaling down if we over-commit? We need flexibility.
[04:58] Jordan Lee: Contracts include a scaling corridor; typically we do +/- 20% permissive changes each quarter with a reconciliation mechanism. We'll reflect that in the draft.
[05:12] Samir Das: On the technical dry-run — we want Redwood to run a smoke test in the EU region with our dataset (anonymized) to validate latency and KV cache behavior before we flip any traffic.
[05:24] Priya Nair: That's doable. We'll need an access-via-bucket pattern or a small containerized sample with fake tokens. Recommend scheduling a dry-run two weeks before GA.
[05:36] Rina Patel: Do you have a benchmark sheet for EU latencies on the 8x A100 configs? The last one I saw had mixed numbers for long-context workloads.
[05:48] Priya Nair: I'll attach the per-model performance matrix for A100 and H100; note that long context with KV cache scales differently — that sheet includes the streaming latency percentiles. Also sometimes transcription labels model names slightly off — we saw references to K/V cache as "KV cash" in older notes.
[06:10] Dr. Maya Chen: (laughs) that explains some of the confusion in the docs.
[06:18] Alex Gomez: Any competitor concerns?
[06:21] Luis Ortega: We're talking to Anthropic on a multi-cloud approach, and evaluating Cohere for embeddings at scale. The difference here is Redwood's ops story and cost controls.
[06:32] Alex Gomez: Good to know, we'll emphasize our Optimize recommendations and the cost per thousand-token comparisons.
[06:40] Priya Nair: For the dry-run we should confirm expected request mix. Luis, can you share the shape: percent chat vs batch, typical sequence lengths?
[06:52] Luis Ortega: Sure, current mix is 60% chat short-turn (<=64 tokens), 25% triage mid (256-512 tokens), 15% long batch (1k-2k) for summarization.
[07:05] Priya Nair: Great that'll guide batching and kernel selection on the runtime. We'll include a recommended config: keep small chat on Hosted Dedicated nodes, route long batches to a dedicated batch pool with higher memory instances.
[07:20] Rina Patel: What about observability retention? We need 12 months for auditability. Is that an add-on?
[07:28] Jordan Lee: Yes longer trace/log retention is an add-on; we can include an enterprise observability package in pricing. It includes token-level cost breakdowns and per-route traces.
[07:40] Samir Das: On KMS — we need HSM-backed keys for certain datasets. Do you integrate with our HSM vendor?
[07:49] Priya Nair: We have integrations for common KMS and support bringing-your-own-HSM in Private deployments. We'll list supported vendors in the security pack.
[07:59] Alex Gomez: Alright, let's recap next steps. We'll deliver the pricing worksheet that compares Hosted Dedicated vs Private EU options, include estimated cost delta, contract terms, and a dry-run checklist. Priya will own the dry-run plan and Jordan will surface contract corridors.
[08:20] Dr. Maya Chen: And we'll review and circle back; Samir will validate the data residency list.
[08:28] Alex Gomez: Perfect. Anything else?
[08:30] Rina Patel: One tiny ask — can Redwood share a sample SLA for throughput percentiles? We want end-to-end numbers for clinical triage.
[08:38] Alex Gomez: We'll include the SLA matrix.
[08:41] (short pause, wrap up)
[08:45] Alex Gomez: Thanks everyone, we'll send the worksheet and security docs by Tuesday.
[08:50] Luis Ortega: Thanks, talk soon.
